text: Last lesson decided when to build a subflow. Now we look at what actually passes between a subflow and the flow that calls it — its Inputs and its Outputs.

A subflow has no Trigger, so it has no record and no event handing it data automatically the way a top-level flow's trigger does. Everything it needs has to be handed to it explicitly. That's what the Inputs section defines — a named, typed list of exactly what the subflow requires. A Notify and Log Manager Decision subflow might define three inputs: a Manager, a reference to a sys underscore user record; a Request Record, a reference to whatever triggered the need for a decision; and a Message, a plain string.

A subflow also usually finishes with information the caller needs back — did the manager approve or reject, and when. That's what the Outputs section defines: a named, typed list of exactly what gets handed back once the subflow completes. The same subflow might define two outputs — a Decision, approved or rejected, and a Decision Date. Without defined outputs, everything that happened inside the subflow would be invisible to whatever called it.

If you've worked with functions in any programming language, this will feel familiar — Inputs are like parameters, Outputs are like a return value. That holds up conceptually, but you're not writing a function signature in code. You're naming each input and output and picking a data type from a dropdown, the same low-code configuration every other part of Flow Designer uses.

Here's how it connects in practice. A flow calls a subflow through a Call Subflow action dropped into its own sequence of steps. The configuration panel shows the subflow's defined inputs, and the flow builder maps its own data pills into each one — the trigger record, a manager field, a message built earlier. Once the subflow finishes, its outputs become new data pills, available in every step after that action — usable in an If-Else on the Decision, or written straight onto a record. Next, a full worked lab: pulling this exact logic out of three real flows.
